title: Compatibility canary orchestra with stubbed tool scenarios and golden seed prompts
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a robust conformance and regression harness that verifies cross-version API compatibility for streaming responses, tool/function calling contracts, and structured output schemas. This work introduces a 'golden seed' prompt corpus (deterministic seeds + edge cases), a stubbed tool oracle that can mimic external tool latencies, errors, and schema violations, and a canary CI pipeline that runs nightly across dedicated runtime variants. The goal is to detect behavioral regressions (including streaming chunk boundaries, function call tokenization changes, and structured-output schema drift) before they reach customers or Dedicated/Private deployments. The harness must be deterministic by default, support targeted fuzzing runs, and emit a compact fingerprint and concordance score for each run to track regressions over time.
acceptance_criteria: A golden prompt suite of ~600 seeds covering common and edge streaming/toolcall/structured-output patterns is checked into the repo and versioned.
A stubbed tool oracle is available for CI that can simulate: success, deterministic error payloads, 100-500ms jitter, and malformed JSON payloads for schema drift tests.
CI job 'canary-orchestra' runs within 30 minutes on the hosted CI image and gates merges to runtime-1.20 with a failing threshold defined in the run config.

Each test run emits a fingerprint file and concordance metric; cross-runtime concordance >= 99% for golden seeds; any drop <98% triggers a failed canary and automated Slack alert to #runtime-canaries.
There is a documented reproduction snippet (curl + seed) for any failing test and at least one linked GitHub PR that fixes a non-flaky failure.
E2E coverage includes streaming chunk loss/resume scenarios, tool-call fallback behavior, and structured-output version compatibility (v1/v2 schemas).
steps: Design golden seed taxonomy and cluster seeds by intent (streaming-only, tool-call, structured-output, mixed).
Implement stubbed-tool service with small python/Go binary that reads a scenario manifest and injects latency/errors.
Add a deterministic harness runner that can execute seeds against multiple runtime variants (hosted, dedicated-sim, private-sim).
Integrate harness into CI as 'canary-orchestra' with matrixed jobs and artifact upload (fingerprints + raw logs).
Add Slack + Opsgenie alerting rules for regressions and publish run results to dashboard (Grafana).
Iterate on seeds and add fuzzers for schema drift and tokenizer boundary cases.
progress_updates: 2025-02-18 - Scoped initial work with PM and Design. Decided to prioritize deterministic golden seeds before broad fuzzing (Ava).

2025-02-22 - Prototype stubbed-tool implemented (python) and can return four behaviors: success, 422 schema error, delayed 250ms, and truncated stream (Ravi). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compat-harness/pull/128
2025-02-25 - First runs on runtime-1.19 vs runtime-1.20-dev showed a 0.8% concordance delta due to streaming-chunk boundary change. Logged investigation notes and opened ENG-67915 for root cause.
2025-02-28 - Design review complete; UX/PM requested clearer failure classification (regression vs flaky vs environmental). Added flaky-detection heuristic to runner.
2025-03-03 - CI job added to nightly pipeline under 'canary-orchestra'. Two test flakes observed; work started to reduce nondeterminism by pinning model seeds and network bandwidth in CI container.
test_matrix: Axes: runtime version (runtime-1.18/1.19/1.20-dev), model variants (base, quantized-8, int4), SDK surface (REST, streaming SDKs: python/node), streaming modes (chunked-bytes, chunked-tokens, long-poll), tool-call modes (sync, async, multiplexed), structured schema versions (v1, v2). Each CI job runs a sub-matrix sampling 150 golden seeds and 50 fuzzed cases.
runbook: If canary fails: 1) Download latest artifacts link from CI job. 2) Run local harness: ./harness/run.sh --seed <seed> --runtime <url> --stubbed-tool=local. 3) Compare fingerprint: jq .fingerprint run/artifacts/latest.json and diff with baseline. 4) If discrepancy reproducible, open a PR with failing seed and add '@runtime-team' to reviewers. 5) If non-reproducible, mark as flaky and add to flake-triage board. Example reproduction: curl -X POST https://ci-runner.internal/run -d '{"seed":"golden/stream/043.json"}'
notes: Tradeoffs: making the harness fully deterministic reduces coverage of real-world network flakiness; we plan separate nightly fuzz runs that re-enable stochastic jitter.
Risk: Flaky tests may create noise for oncall. We will invest two cycles in robust flake detection heuristics before widening the canary to block merges.

Follow-ups: 1) Add dedicated metrics for function-call argument canonicalization differences. 2) Expand golden seed corpus to include non-English tokenization edge cases. 3) Add a lightweight browser-based viewer for streaming trace replays (UX request).
